question: How long does vermicompost take to be ready and which earthworm is preferred?
question_en: How long does vermicompost take to be ready and which earthworm is preferred?
answer_en: Vermicompost takes 45 to 50 days to be ready. Eisenia foetida is preferred because it multiplies quickly and converts material into compost in 45–50 days. It is a surface feeder and produces cocoons every 3 days.
answer: Vermicompost takes 45 to 50 days to be ready. Eisenia foetida is preferred because it multiplies quickly and converts material into compost in 45–50 days. It is a surface feeder and produces cocoons every 3 days.

retrieved.text: Eisenia foetida (red earthworm) is preferred because it multiplies quickly; it is a surface feeder and converts material into compost in 45 to 50 days. Eudrilus eugeniae (night crawler) and Perionyx excavatus are also used. E. foetida is 3-10 cm long, matures in 50-55 days and produces a cocoon every 3 days.

retrieved.title: Vermicompost production and use
retrieved.text: 1. Mix cow dung and chopped dry leaves in a 3:1 ratio and let it partly decompose for 15 to 20 days. 2. Lay a 15-20 cm layer of chopped dry leaves or grass at the bottom of the bed. 3. Fill the bed (6 x 2 x 2 feet) with 1.5 to 2.0 quintals of partly decomposed material. 4. Release 1,500 to 2,000 red earthworms on the upper layer. 5. Sprinkle water immediately and keep the bed moist by daily sprinkling; cover with gunny bags or polythene. 6. Turn the material once after 30 days for aeration. 7. The compost is ready in 45 to 50 days; output is about three-quarters of the raw material weight.

retrieved.title: Vermicompost production and use

Lay a 15-20 cm layer of chopped dry leaves or grass at the bottom of the bed. 3. Fill the bed (6 x 2 x 2 feet) with 1.5 to 2.0 quintals of partly decomposed material. 4. Release 1,500 to 2,000 red earthworms on the upper layer. 5. Sprinkle water immediately and keep the bed moist by daily sprinkling; cover with gunny bags or polythene. 6. Turn the material once after 30 days for aeration. 7. The compost is ready in 45 to 50 days; output is about three-quarters of the raw material weight.

retrieved.text: SRI is more suitable for the dry season with assured irrigation. Establishment is difficult during heavy rains such as the north-east monsoon in Tamil Nadu. Hybrids and varieties with heavy tillering are preferred.

retrieved.title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) crop insurance
retrieved.text: The scheme covers crop loss from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Localized risks covered include hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloud burst and natural fire. Post-harvest losses caused by cyclone, cyclonic or unseasonal rain and hailstorm are covered for up to 14 days after harvest, when the crop is kept in the field to dry. Damage by wild animals is an optional add-on that a state may choose to offer at its own cost.

retrieved.title: Rice main-field nutrient management (transplanted rice)
retrieved.section: Blanket fertilizer recommendations (kg N, P2O5, K2O per hectare)
retrieved.text: When soil-test based recommendations cannot be followed, the blanket doses are: - Short-duration varieties in the dry season: 150:50:50 in the Cauvery delta and Coimbatore tract, and 120:40:40 in other tracts. - Medium and long-duration varieties in the wet season: 150:50:50. - Hybrid rice: 175:60:60. - Low-nitrogen-responsive cultivars such as Improved White Ponni: 75:50:50. For Ponni, nitrogen is given in three splits at active tillering, panicle initiation and heading, along with green leaf manure or farmyard manure.
